The test image shows a very young soybean seedling just emerging from wet/moist soil. The seedling appears to have a damaged/discolored hypocotyl and seed. This points to a seed/seedling disease. Top candidates: Pythium_damping_off, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora.

Let me view reference images one at a time.
This Pythium reference is very similar to the test image - wet soil, early seedling stage, similar field conditions. Let me check Rhizoctonia next.
Rhizoctonia reference shows older plant with stem canker - less similar to the test. Let me check Phytophthora.
This Pythium whole plant image is very similar to the test - rotted seedling in wet dark soil. Let me explore one more class (Fusarium) to be thorough before settling.
Fusarium doesn't match at all. I need 4 more views from different classes. Let me check Phytophthora, Charcoal_Rot, Soybean_Cyst_Nematode, and Septoria_brown_spot.

I've now used all 8 views across 6 classes. The analysis is clear:

**Test image analysis:**
- Very young soybean seedling at emergence, lying partially flat in wet, dark soil
- Greenish hypocotyl/cotyledon with brownish damaged root visible
- Crop residue in background, wet field conditions

**Comparison results:**
- Pythium_damping_off (views 1, 3, 8): All three reference images are strikingly similar - same wet dark soil, same crop residue, same collapsed/rotted early seedling appearance. View 8 (seed/45) is nearly identical to the test.
- Rhizoctonia: Shows older plant with distinct stem canker - not matching
- Fusarium: Shows mature canopy - not matching
- Phytophthora: Field-level view of older wilting plants - not matching
- Charcoal_Rot: Mature plant field stand - not matching
- Soybean_Cyst_Nematode: Root system closeup of established plant - not matching

Pythium_damping_off is a clear match: soft rot of seeds/seedlings in wet soil conditions, collapsed seedling at emergence stage, exactly consistent with all three Pythium reference images.
